subtopics.title: India-Japan Partnership Beyond the Summit
subtopics.summary: Japan's support for Subhas Chandra Bose's Azad Hind Fauj, formed to fight colonial rule, is a historical link in the relationship. Japan is India's largest official development assistance donor and its fifth largest investor. The partnership also covers joint military exercises, a lunar space mission and several global initiatives.
facts: Subhas Chandra Bose established Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) with Japanese support to fight colonial rule
Japan is the 5th largest investor in India (FDI)
Japan is India's largest Official Development Assistance donor since 1958
Joint exercises: Malabar (naval, with US and Australia), Milan (multilateral naval), JIMEX (navy), Dharma Guardian (army), SHINYUU Maitri (air force)
Space: Lunar Polar Exploration Mission (LUPEX), also called Chandrayaan-5
Global programmes: International Solar Alliance; Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure; LeadIT; India-Japan-Australia Supply Chain Resilience Initiative
Frameworks listed under Skill-Up: Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, SAGAR, MAHASAGAR, QUAD, ASEAN, BIMSTEC, UNCLOS, G4 for UNSC Reform

subtopics.title: Green Hydrogen and the National Green Hydrogen Mission
subtopics.summary: Hydrogen is the most common element in nature but exists only in combination with other elements, so it must be extracted from compounds such as water. Green hydrogen is made by splitting water through electrolysis using an electrolyser powered by renewable energy, and the booklet says it is not commercially viable at present. The National Green Hydrogen Mission, with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy as nodal ministry, aims to decarbonise sectors and build domestic manufacturing.
facts: Hydrogen is the most common element in nature but exists only in combination with other elements
Hydrogen has to be extracted from naturally occurring compounds such as water
Green hydrogen: water is split by electrolysis using an electrolyser powered by renewable energy
Green hydrogen is not commercially viable at present
Nodal ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Objectives: decarbonise energy, industrial and mobility sectors; develop indigenous manufacturing; create export opportunities for green hydrogen and its derivatives
SIGHT: Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition Programme
SHIP: Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership (PPP for R&D)
Expected by 2030: Rs 1 lakh crore in fossil fuel import savings
